Quickstart

Source: vignettes/quickstart.Rmd
quickstart.Rmd

Create a task, fit a DR-learner, and predict conditional average treatment effects. The example uses simulated data and simple mean learners, with cross-fitting and model selection disabled.

library(hte3)
library(sl3)

data <- hte3_example_data(n = 120, seed = 1)

task <- hte_task(
  data = data,
  modifiers = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  confounders = c("W1", "W2", "W3"),
  treatment = "A",
  outcome = "Y",
  propensity_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  outcome_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  mean_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_fit = FALSE
)

model <- fit_cate(
  task,
  method = "dr",
  base_learner = Lrnr_mean$new(),
  cross_validate = FALSE
)

head(predict(model, data))
#> [1] 1.027376 1.027376 1.027376 1.027376 1.027376 1.027376
summary(model)
#> <summary.hte3_model>
#>   Target: CATE
#>   Engine: sl3
#>   Method: dr
#>   Cross-validated: no
#>   Rows: 120
#>   Modifiers: W1, W2, W3
#>   Treatment variable: A

Cross-fitting and model selection

Use these arguments to control nuisance estimation and model selection:

  • cross_fit in hte_task() controls nuisance estimation.
  • cross_validate in fit_cate() or fit_crr() controls selection across candidate HTE learners.

Set cross_fit = TRUE to estimate each observation’s nuisance values using other folds. Set cross_validate = TRUE to compare candidate HTE learners.

Next steps

  • Treatment effects: choose among DR-, R-, T-, and EP-learners.
  • Risk ratios: estimate relative effects for non-negative outcomes.
  • Causal forests: use grf_cate() and grf_crr().
  • Using sl3 directly: construct and train custom learners.
